successors.name: Kingdom of Mysore
successors.text: the Zamorin's lands: Calicut, Ponnani and Thiruvanchikkulam

ledger.x: 1405: 'the Perumpadappu ruler moved to Kochi in 1405 after Calicut took Thiruvanchikkulam' (Kodungallur).
1498: 'The Zamorin built a fort at Ponnani in 1498' (Vasco da Gama landed at Calicut that year); Ponnani's Thrikkavil Kovilakam was the clan's 'second home'.
27 April 1766: Hyder Ali defeated the Zamorin and absorbed Calicut; the 117th Zamorin 'committed suicide' by fire ('Annexed by Mysore', table).

wars.name: Zamorin's wars with the Portuguese
wars.outcome: Intermittent war from the Zamorin's 1502 demand that the Portuguese factors leave Kochi to the peace sued for in 1540 by Chinna Kutti Ali, the Zamorin's admiral; the page names the 1526 siege of Calicut and gives no treaty year.

wars.name: Hyder Ali's conquest of Malabar
wars.outcome: Hyder Ali took Calicut 'in a bloody battle' and the Zamorin killed himself on 27 April 1766.

certainty.note: A coastal chiefdom with no surveyed frontier; the pages give places (Kozhikode, Thiruvanchikkulam, Ponnani) and a peak extent from Kozhikode Kollam to Panthalayini Kollam (Koyilandy) without a year, so every shape is a disc round those…
